highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves WebAssembly packaging, Android rendering synchronization, and managed graphics memory efficiency.
highlights_body: Apple targets now require newer operating-system versions, and front-buffered streams release managed references reliably.

breaking.title: Apple deployment requirements raised
breaking.body: iOS and tvOS targets now require version 14.0, and native macOS binaries target macOS 11.0. Retarget applications and update supported-device requirements before upgrading.

bullets.lead: WebAssembly WebGPU support is packaged with the native library
bullets.detail: The emdawnwebgpu implementation is compiled into libSkiaSharp, so modern .NET WebAssembly applications no longer pass its C++ source and compile flags through their final link.

bullets.lead: Linux uses its bundled HarfBuzz symbols locally
bullets.detail: Linux native assets bind HarfBuzz functions from the bundled library, avoiding interference from similarly named symbols supplied by the host environment.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: GLTextureView synchronizes texture rendering with display refresh, improving the timing of Android texture presentation.

bullets.lead: Managed pixel and text paths avoid temporary allocations
bullets.detail: Pixel-copy image creation and common HarfBuzz text and feature conversions use direct or pooled buffers where possible, reducing allocation pressure without changing their results.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams release retained managed streams
bullets.detail: Disposing a front-buffered managed stream now clears its managed stream reference even when the caller retains ownership of that stream.
